book.title: Focus: The Hidden Driver of Excellence
book.author: Daniel Goleman

confidence_note: Three-way split (inner, other, outer focus), empathy types, systems awareness (detect and map patterns, zoom in and out), willpower techniques and leadership use come from publisher/summary sources (Mindful interview, Shortform overview); book text not read. Old-text claims about leaders with only one focus being 'blind', and that the three are built by practice rather than innate, were dropped or softened. Old text said 'system focus' for the third; the book calls it outer focus (systems awareness).
facts: Goleman divides attention into inner focus, other focus and outer focus.

Inner focus attunes us to intuitions and guiding values. It includes self-awareness (living by values and purpose, following the gut, noticing where attention goes, perceiving accurately how others see you) and willpower (resisting instant gratification for a long-term goal).
Willpower techniques: shift focus away from the desired object, focus on something else, keep a longer-term goal in mind.

Other focus smooths connections with people; empathy comes in three kinds: cognitive (understanding what another thinks without feeling it), emotional (feeling what they feel), empathic concern (compassion that moves you to help).
Outer focus lets us navigate the larger world; systems awareness means detecting and mapping a system's patterns and zooming between details and big picture.
Goleman argues large-scale problems such as climate change need systems awareness and long-view attention.
For a leader: inner focus to assess strengths and weaknesses and manage impact; other focus to listen and sense the team's energy; outer focus to decide what to focus on and ignore.
Goleman argues that to lead well the three must be integrated.
scene_details: zooming between detail and big picture
tension: Attention can face three directions, and a leader mostly uses one.
opening_idea: Attention has directions, not just strength.

lessons.idea: Before a decision, check which of the three directions you skipped.
lessons.anchor: Inner, other and outer focus each supply different information (own gut, team's energy, larger pattern).
lessons.everyday_example_idea: A cafe owner deciding on a second branch looks only at figures.

reflect_final: When you make a big decision, does your attention usually go to your own feelings, to the people affected, or to the wider setting around it?

use_cases.situation: A decision is about to be made in a team meeting
use_cases.move: Ask what we feel, what the people carrying it out think, and what it changes later.
Name what you understand they feel and check it.
Check your inner voice first, then the figures.

pocket_idea: Attention faces inward, toward others and outward to the system; ask which one you forgot.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Goleman's third focus is the wide one: seeing the system.
